title: Cozy game UI design help
author: Smart_Breakfast_6165
selftext:
Hello everybody,

I am trying to develop a game using Claude Code. I am on a laptop equipped with 32 GB of RAM and a 4070 with 16 GB of VRAM, and I set it up with both 9router and OmniRoute to use free models plus good local ones like qwen3.5:9b.

My goal is to develop a cozy/puzzle/management game focused on the three members of a family of characters and their friends. The idea is to be able to switch characters to play with their daily activities, plus making them interact to gain relationship points which unlock different story modes and other playing characters.

I more or less was able to implement a playable baseline, thanks to a full game design document and MCP access to a local ComfyUI instance with a local model for image generation. My main concern is the UI, though, which keeps being absolutely clunky and messy. I know I am missing something, maybe in the way I am planning the steps or something like that, but I don't know what. Can you help me identifying my missteps?

replies.author: Smart_Breakfast_6165
replies.body:
Thanks for the suggestions! The bulk of the work is carried out by a bunch of models such as deepseekV4-flash, the local ones are a fallback for API exhaustion.
I had a sketch for the UI, yes, I fed it to Claude, it seemed able to understand it but failed to match it in any way. Maybe Claude Code isn't the right choice, or maybe I am getting something wrong...

comments.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
comments.body: How are you currently building the UI?

replies.author: Smart_Breakfast_6165
replies.body: As of now, I let Claude decide what to do using the Godot game engine.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Text_347
replies.body:
From what i've learned, ai is bad at interpreting what you're wanting if you give it too long of a leash. Tell it exactly what you want, and be extremely specific. If there's something off and it's having trouble fixing it, be more specific about what you want fixed. "The UI feels clunky" won't always lead to the best results. I would do something along the lines of:  
"Rework the ui to simplify the ux. I want the ui to have a simple hover animation and feel responsive without being overbearing. Use xyz as the color theme and make sure it all feels cohesive and connected with the rest of the game"

comments.author: DomiGamingOfficial
comments.body: Install a design skill. Claude can give you a list of options. Then upload screen shots from the game. It can give you cleaner options a d suggestions.
